typography.actual_price: text-4xl md:text-5xl font-fredoka font-bold tracking-tight text-[#1D3557]
typography.badge_text: text-xs font-bold font-outfit uppercase tracking-widest text-[#1D3557]

visual_enhancers.strikethrough_style: Do NOT use standard CSS line-through. Use a custom absolute span element: `h-[3px] bg-[#EE6C4D] -translate-y-1/2 -rotate-3` to look like a playful, deliberate marker cross-out.
visual_enhancers.badge_style: Neo-brutalist pill: `px-3 py-1 rounded-full border-2 border-[#1D3557] shadow-[2px_2px_0px_0px_#1D3557] -rotate-2 transform-gpu`.

layouts.component_structure: Flex column for the overall container (`flex flex-col gap-1 items-start`). Top row contains the discount badge. Bottom row is a flex container (`flex flex-row items-baseline gap-3 mt-1`) holding the actual price and original price.
layouts.spacing: Maintain `gap-3` between the actual price and the original price. Align them using `items-baseline` so the numbers sit on the same visual baseline.

motion.badge_hover: Hovering the pricing area can cause the badge to slightly rotate to 0deg or scale up (`hover:scale-105 hover:rotate-0 transition-transform duration-200`).

accessibility.strikethrough: The custom strikethrough span MUST have `aria-hidden="true"`. The original price span MUST include an aria-label, e.g., `aria-label="Original price: 120000 rupees"`.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build a reusable React/JS component or HTML/Tailwind block for the PricingOffer that can be embedded in both the Money Masters batch price cards and the platform subscription pricing cards.
Do NOT use standard text-decoration for the strikethrough. Use the relative/absolute span trick described in visual_enhancers for the playful brand look.
Make the badge text customizable (e.g., 'SAVE 25%' or 'LIMITED TIME OFFER').
Ensure the component scales down nicely on mobile (use responsive text classes).
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur) where appropriate.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: `transition: all`. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add `.App { text-align: center; }` in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations. Static = dead.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a `data-testid` attribute to facilitate robust automated testing.
